questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Heap, stacks, and static allocation”?
options: Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
Release allocated memory and plan long-lived objects deliberately.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
questions.answer: Release allocated memory and plan long-lived objects deliberately.
questions.explanation:
Release allocated memory and plan long-lived objects deliberately.
Why: Every FreeRTOS task consumes its own stack; tasks, queues, and timers may also allocate from the kernel heap. Creation can fail when memory is exhausted, while stack overflow can corrupt state. Measure stack high-water marks and minimum heap, and consider static allocation where supported; do not copy demo sizes into production without measurement.
